correctness.rationale: Nilpotent elements have precisely two forced zero diagonal residues in the two-block endomorphism algebra, and are parametrized by 4m-5 independent field coefficients. The exact rank-preserving reduction identifies the full ordinary rank with that of a constrained 2-by-2 matrix over F_q[t]/(t^(m-1)). Its modulo-t residues have explicit invertible, rank-one and zero counts. Each rank-one Schur complement ranges uniformly over the maximal ideal; the rank-zero layer descends to an unrestricted shorter 2-by-2 ring. These disjoint counts give the exact G and P polynomial recursions, with correct m=2 boundary. The highest rank is equivalent to two nonzero off-diagonal residues, giving exact regular-nilpotent count and open geometric stratum. A standalone independent finite enumeration confirms all coefficients over q=2,3,4 in six settings; it is not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is a complete finite-field ordinary-rank multiplicity formula for nilpotent commuting matrices with consecutive Jordan lengths. Oblak 2007 gives maximum possible nilpotency index, not rank counts. Hua 2023 has canonical forms for unequal two-block nilpotent pairs, but in inspected full sections 2-3 does not give this polynomial or finite-field fiber counts; deriving them from a more general orbit classification would require further counting. Basili–Iarrobino and Košir–Oblak address generic commuting Jordan types, not all finite-field rank multiplicities. A neighboring equal-block classification addresses different parameters. Published mathematical literature and scholarly research-record searches did not give an identical formula. This is a best-knowledge priority conclusion with acknowledged residual risk.
residual_risks: The strong 2023 canonical-form theorem may encode the answer through unstated orbit-size calculations; complete derivation comparison was not established.
Older truncated-polynomial matrix enumeration sources under alternate terminology may contain the same rank polynomial.
Only an abstract was read for some relevant articles; an inaccessible source was not classified as NOT_COVERING.

value.rationale: The theorem provides every finite-field ordinary-rank stratum of a canonical nilpotent centralizer family, not only generic Jordan data or the top index. Its universal (1-1/q)^2 regular probability, simple explicit geometric top stratum, and full rank-polynomial recursion provide meaningful refinements of classic questions on nilpotent commuting pairs. It is natural across all consecutive block lengths and prime powers; it does not claim a full Jordan-type census.
